FARRA:v2p217/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p217/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p217/r2.claim: The object of يدعو من دون الله is idols.
FARRA:v2p217/r2.anchor: يدعوا من دون الله [12] يعنى الأصنام

NAHHAS:v3p88/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p88/r3.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p88/r3.claim: He glosses ḥarf as the long edge or side.
NAHHAS:v3p88/r3.anchor:
جل وعز إياه وأمره بلعنه وأن لا حظ له في غنيمة ولا ثناء وخسر الآخرة بأن لا ثواب له فيها
12 قال الفراء أي الطويل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p137/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p137/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p137/r3.claim: The unstable worshipper then invokes besides God what can neither harm nor benefit, truly relying on something other than God and abandoning the exclusive plea for divine help.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p137/r3.anchor: أي يعبد حقيقة أومجازا مع التجدد والاستمرار بالاعتماد على غير الله

DURR-FULL:v6p15/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p15/r2.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v6p15/r2.claim: The idol cannot harm one who disobeys it or benefit one who obeys; its harm comes in the afterlife, and it is a bad protector.
DURR-FULL:v6p15/r2.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {يدعو من دون الله ما لا يضره} إن عصاه في الدنيا {وما لا ينفعه} إن أطاعه وهو الصنم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p110/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p110/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p110/r3.claim: The objects called upon are idols; yadʿu can mean worshipping them or invoking them in distress.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p110/r3.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ما لا يضره يريد الأوثان، ومعنى يدعوا يعبد، ويدعو أيضا في ملماته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p402/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p402/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p402/r3.claim: Those who invoke idols and rivals seek help, victory, and provision from things that neither harm nor benefit; their harm in this world is nearer than any benefit, and in the next it is certain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p402/r3.anchor: أي: من الأصنام والأنداد، يستغيث بها ويستنصرها ويسترزقها، وهي لا تنفعه ولا تضره

JISHUMI:v7p4920/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4920/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4920/r4.claim: Ashir means companion, spouse, or one who associates with another.

MUQATIL:22:11-12/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:11-12/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:11-12/r6.claim: The idol worshipper invokes what cannot harm him in this world if neglected or benefit him in the Hereafter if worshipped; this is far-reaching misguidance.
MUQATIL:22:11-12/r6.anchor: { يدعوا } يعنى يعبد { من دون الله } يعنى الصنم { ما لا يضره } فى الدنيا إن لم يعبده

RAZI-FULL:v23p13/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p13/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p13/r7.claim: The one who calls on something besides God that neither harms nor benefits is most likely a polytheist worshipping idols, which makes the passage unlikely to concern a Jew.
RAZI-FULL:v23p13/r7.anchor: الأقرب أنه المشرك الذي يعبد الأوثان وهذا كالدلالة على أن الآية لم ترد في اليهودي

RAZI-FULL:v23p13/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p13/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p13/r8.claim: Razi says the passage likely concerns polytheists who attached themselves to the Messenger hypocritically.
RAZI-FULL:v23p13/r8.anchor: في المشركين الذين انقطعوا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.claim: One dating view holds that the surah is Madinan except verses 52–55, which are Makkan.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.anchor: Some say it is Madinan except for vv. 52–55, which are Makkan (IK)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.claim: Another dating view holds that the surah is Makkan except verses 19–22, which are Madinan.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.anchor: others say it is Makkan except for vv.19–22, which are from the Madinan period (Q)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.claim: Most authorities regard the surah as containing both Makkan and Madinan verses.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.anchor: Most say it is a mix of Makkan and Madinan verses (Q)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.claim: A tradition calls the surah remarkable because it came at night and by day, on journeys and at home, in war and peace, and includes abrogating and abrogated as well as clear and allegorical verses.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.anchor: and it has both muḥkam (unambiguous) and mutashābih (symbolic or allegorical) verses (Q)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r7.claim: The passage contrasts the misguided and righteous through a garden parable and their respective afterlife reward or punishment.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r7.anchor: describing their reward or punishment in the Hereafter (vv.8–25)

TABATABAI:22:11-15/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:11-15/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:11-15/r2.claim: An idol cannot harm or benefit because it lacks awareness and will; the harm and loss its worshipper suffers comes from the worshipper's own act.
TABATABAI:22:11-15/r2.anchor: فإنه لفقده الشعور والإرادة لا يتوجه منه إلى عابده نفع أو ضرر والذي يصيب عابده من ضرر وخسران فإنما يصيبه من ناحية العبادة

TABRISI:22:11-15/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:11-15/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:11-15/r6.claim: The syntax of لمن ضره is disputed: one account fronts an emphatic oath lām and supplies an implicit pronoun with يدعو; other analyses construe the phrase as a new subject and predicate or as the object of يدعو.
TABRISI:22:11-15/r6.anchor: اختلف الناس في تفسير هذه اللام فقال البصريون والكوفيون

TABRISI:22:11-15#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:11-15#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:22:11-15#2/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj supplies three syntactic possibilities for يدعو لمن ضره: the lām may be a postponed emphatic particle, يدعو may be circumstantial with an implied object, or ذلك may be a relative pronoun whose clause is its object.
TABRISI:22:11-15#2/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج: وفيه وجه آخر وهو أن يكون يدعو في معنى يقول

TABRISI:22:11-15#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:11-15#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:11-15#2/r2.claim: The author explains that يدعو may mean ‘calls out/says’ or ‘names’; in the latter case the cited Ibn Ahmar verse shows a thing being called by a name.
TABRISI:22:11-15#2/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون يدعو في معنى يسمى

TABRISI:22:11-15#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:11-15#2/r3.speaker: عنترة
TABRISI:22:11-15#2/r3.claim: Antara's line in which warriors call to him illustrates يدعو in the sense of calling or addressing someone.

THALABI:v7p9#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p9#2/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p9#2/r10.claim: Calling on anything besides God is useless: it can neither harm when disobeyed nor benefit when obeyed, and this is far misguidance.
THALABI:v7p9#2/r10.anchor: يدعوا من دون الله ما لا يضره إن عصاه وما لا ينفعه إن أطاعه

THALABI:v7p9#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p9#2/r11.speaker: بعض النحاة
THALABI:v7p9#2/r11.claim: Some grammarians treat the lām in يدعو لمن as an extra particle; Ibn Masud's reading omits it.
THALABI:v7p9#2/r11.anchor: هي صلة مجازها: يدعو من ضره أقرب من نفعه، وهكذا قرأها ابن مسعود

THALABI:v7p9#2/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p9#2/r12.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
THALABI:v7p9#2/r12.claim: They say the lām is displaced later in the sentence, yielding the sense that he invokes one whose harm is nearer than his benefit.
THALABI:v7p9#2/r12.anchor: وزعم الفراء والزجاج أن اللام معناها التأخير

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:8-12/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:8-12/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:8-12/r6.claim: The idols invoked apart from God neither harm their worshippers when disobeyed nor benefit them when obeyed; relying on them is distant misguidance.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:8-12/r6.anchor: ذلك هو الضلال البعيد } الذهاب عن الحق

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p357/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p357/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p357/r2.claim: The object invoked besides God is an idol that can neither harm nor benefit, and this is distant error.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p357/r2.anchor: قوله: {يدعو من دون الله ما لا يضره وما لا ينفعه} [الحج: 12] يعني الوثن. {ذلك هو الضلال البعيد} [الحج: 12]

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r3.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r3.claim: Commentators offer linguistic explanations for the apparent difference between verse 12’s beings that can neither harm nor benefit and verse 13’s beings whose harm is nearer than their benefit.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r3.anchor: Bu iki âyet arasındaki bağla ilgili dil bilgisine dayalı birçok izahın yanı sıra

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r5.speaker: bir yorum
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r5.claim: Another interpretation keeps the reference to idols: idols themselves neither help nor harm, but worshipping them causes harm by costing their devotees the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r5.anchor: Putların kendileri yarar sağlamadıkları gibi zarar da veremezler, ama onlara kulluk edilmesi zarara yol açar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r7.claim: Even after turning from God, these people cannot stop worshipping and supplicating; they turn to beings that are useless or likely to harm them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:11/r7.anchor: bu kimseler yine de “kulluk etme ve yakarma” ihtiyacından kendilerini alıkoyamamakta, ama bu defa ya hiçbir yararı veya zararı dokunmayacak

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p179/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p179/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p179/r1.claim: The verb ‘invoke’ includes praying, pleading, beseeching, and seeking help or mercy; assigning another being authority to harm or benefit is polytheism, since only God controls this and all reliance should be on Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p179/r1.anchor: If someone is invoked thinking that he has the authority to cause harm or benefit, then this is polytheism.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p179/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p179/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p179/r2.claim: The parable in 22:73 shows the extreme error of seeking refuge with beings unable even to create a fly or recover what it steals; fleeing God’s trial thus ends in Hell.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p179/r2.anchor: Those who you invoke besides God cannot even create a fly in spite of all of them trying to.

BURSEVI:v6p7#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p7#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p7#3/r1.claim: The clause resumes the account of the apostate polytheist's great loss: he worships something besides God.
BURSEVI:v6p7#3/r1.anchor: استئناف مبين لعظم الخسران فيكون الضمير راجعا إلى المرتد المشرك

BURSEVI:v6p7#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p7#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p7#3/r2.claim: The object worshipped can neither harm the worshipper if left alone nor benefit him when worshipped; the repeated ما underscores that it is an inert object.

BURSEVI:v6p7#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p7#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p7#3/r3.claim: Calling this worship remote misguidance is a metaphor for a traveler lost in wilderness whose route grows longer and farther from the path.
BURSEVI:v6p7#3/r3.anchor: مستعارا من ضلال من أبعد في التيه ضالا عن الطريق

SULAMI:v2p19/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p19/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p19/r1.claim: Whoever leans on anything besides the Real relies on what harms rather than benefits; whoever relies on God relies on the source of everything.
SULAMI:v2p19/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : من ركن إلى شيء سوى الحق فقد ركن إلى ما يضره ولا ينفعه

SULAMI:v2p19#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p19#2/r1.speaker: السياري
SULAMI:v2p19#2/r1.claim: If God decrees someone's humiliation from the beginning, no one can honor him; the garment of Truth remains unchanged forever.
SULAMI:v2p19#2/r1.anchor: قال السيارى : من قدر الله عليه الإهانة في السبق لا يقدر أحد على كرامته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p215/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p215/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p215/r1.claim: The clause about invoking other than God is circumstantial to the subject of انقلب in 22:11.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p215/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p215/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p215/r2.claim: Mentioning harm before benefit hints that the wavering person abandons Islam to escape perceived harm, imagining Islam caused it and idols are angry; the following clause mocks this mistaken appeal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p215/r2.anchor: فعاد إلى عبادة الأصنام حاسبا أنها لا تضره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p215/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p215/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p215/r3.claim: The idols neither cause harm nor bring benefit, so asking them to remove distress and secure advantage is a mistake.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p215/r3.anchor: أنها لا تفعل ما يجلب ضرا ولا ما يجلب نفعا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p215/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p215/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p215/r4.claim: ذلك points to the invocation; its demonstrative, separating pronoun, and restriction work as in 22:11, while البعيد marks idolatry as an extreme degree of error because the objects have no utility.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p215/r4.anchor: والبعيد : المتجاوز الحد المعروف في مدى الضلال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p411/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p411/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p411/r1.claim: The apostate worships what neither harms him if he does not worship it nor benefits him if he obeys it; this is remote misguidance, far from the truth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p411/r1.anchor: هذا المرتد أي يعبد مالا يضره إن لم يعبده ولا ينفعه إن أطاعة

JISHUMI:v7p4922/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r1.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r1.claim: Grammatically, “that” is an object of “calls” and functions like a relative pronoun; the phrase about the one whose harm is nearer begins a new clause, or “that” may be nominative with “a wretched protector” as its predicate.
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r1.anchor: وموضع (ذلك) نصب ب (يدعو)، وهو بمعنى (الذي)، كأنه قيل

JISHUMI:v7p4922/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r10.claim: The powerless objects are idols; alternatively, obedience to them brings no benefit and disobedience brings no harm. The worshipper turns to idols or leaders whose harm is nearer than their benefit.
JISHUMI:v7p4922/r10.anchor: يعني الأوثان لا تنفع ولا تضر، وقيل: لا ينفعه إن أطاعه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p97#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p97#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p97#5/r1.claim: After apostasy, the idol neither harms if left unserved nor benefits if worshipped; this is far error.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p97#5/r1.anchor: ﴿ يدعو من دون الله ﴾ يعني الصنم فإنه بعد الردة يفعل كذلك ﴿ ما لا يضره ﴾ ان لم يعبده

QURTUBI-FULL:22:12/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:12/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:12/r1.claim: The verse describes someone reverting to disbelief and worshipping an idol that can neither harm nor benefit him.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:12/r1.anchor: هذا الذي يرجع إلى الكفر يعبد الصنم الذي لا ينفع ولا يضر

QURTUBI-FULL:22:12/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:12/r2.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:22:12/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ glosses al-ḍalāl al-baʿīd as long error.

STUDYQURAN:22:12/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:12/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:22:12/r1.claim: Commentators usually understand these verses as referring to idols and false gods, often described as neither harming nor benefiting their worshippers.
STUDYQURAN:22:12/r1.anchor: These verses are usually thought to refer to idols and false gods, which are often described as something that neither harms nor benefits

TAB-FULL:v16p476/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p476/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p476/r1.claim: When a person worshipping God precariously meets a trial and apostatizes, he calls on idols that cannot harm him if neglected in this life or benefit him in the next; this is a remote departure from God's path.
TAB-FULL:v16p476/r1.anchor: ارتد عن دين الله، يدعو من دون الله آلهة لا تضره

TAB-FULL:v16p476/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p476/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p476/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses the passage as a person disbelieving after having believed.
TAB-FULL:v16p476/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {يدعو من دون الله ما لا يضره وما لا ينفعه "} [الحج: 12] يكفر بعد إيمانه

ZAJJAJ:v3p414#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p414#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p414#2/r1.claim: The one invoked besides God is an idol that neither hears nor sees nor benefits nor harms.
ZAJJAJ:v3p414#2/r1.anchor: يعنى يدعو الوثن الذي لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا ينفع ولا يضر

ASAD-NOTES:22:12#n11/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:22:12#n11/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:22:12#n11/r1.claim: People who do not commit fully to their professed faith may assign decisive influence over destiny to real or imagined forces, thereby granting them divine qualities.
ASAD-NOTES:22:12#n11/r1.anchor: attribute to all manner of extraneous forces, be they real or imaginary, a decisive "influence" on his own destiny

ASAD-NOTES:22:12#n12/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:22:12#n12/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:22:12#n12/r1.claim: The literal wording is “this, this is the far-away straying”; Asad refers to his explanation of this paraphrase at 14:18.
ASAD-NOTES:22:12#n12/r1.anchor: "this, this (dhalika huwa) is the straying far-away"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p289/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p289/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p289/r1.claim: The person returning to unbelief worships things besides God, namely stones, which neither harm him if he does not worship them nor benefit him if he obeys them; this is far from truth and right guidance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p289/r1.anchor: هذا المرتد يدعو (¬2) راجعا إلى الكفر يعبد سوى الله {ما لا يضره} في معاش إن لم يعبده، ولا ينفعه إن أطاعه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p124#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p124#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p124#3/r1.claim: The clause about worshipping other than God may be a new sentence exposing another fault, explaining the scale of the loss, or a circumstantial clause from the person who turned away, with the preceding material parenthetical.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p124#3/r1.anchor: قيل استئناف نافع عليه بعض قبائحه وقيل استئناف مبين لعظم الخسران

ALUSI-FULL:v17p124#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p124#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p124#3/r2.claim: These readings make the verse unlikely to describe a Jew, since Jews do not worship idols even though they took rabbis and monks as lords.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p124#3/r2.anchor: فهو يبعد كون الآية في أحد من اليهود لأنهم لا يدعون الأصنام

ALUSI-FULL:v17p124#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p124#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p124#3/r3.claim: The objects are apparently idols; supplication means worshipping, beyond God, what cannot harm if left unserved or benefit if worshipped.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p124#3/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن المدعو الأصنام لمكان ما في قوله تعالى ( ما لا يضره وما لا ينفعه (

ALUSI-FULL:v17p124#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p124#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p124#3/r4.claim: Alternatively, supplication means calling upon a lifeless thing to rescue the caller from affliction, although it cannot harm or benefit; repeating ma indicates an inanimate object.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p124#3/r4.anchor: وجوز أن يراد بالدعاء النداء أي ينادي لأجل تخليصه مما أصابه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p124#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p124#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p124#3/r5.claim: Far error is a metaphor for wandering far into a wilderness, away from the right path.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p124#3/r5.anchor: عن الحق والهدى مستعار من ضلال من أبعد في التيه ضالا عن الطريق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p369/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p369/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p369/r1.claim: The idol neither harms the worshipper if he abandons its worship nor benefits him if he worships it; this is far from truth and right guidance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p369/r1.anchor: إن عصاه ولم يعبده، {وما لا ينفعه} إن أطاعه وعبده، {ذلك هو الضلال البعيد}

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:12/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:12/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:12/r1.claim: They worship an inert thing besides God that can neither harm nor benefit; this is far error from the goal, like wandering astray in the wilderness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:12/r1.anchor: يعبد جمادا لا يضر بنفسه ولا ينفع. { ذلك هو الضلال البعيد } عن المقصد مستعار من ضلال من أبعد في التيه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p137#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p137#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p137#2/r1.claim: Everything other than God is beneath the rank of the one possessing all perfection; worship is merited by chosen action, not by compelled natural behavior.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p137#2/r1.anchor: كل ما سوى الله دنه , نبه على ذلك بقوله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p137#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p137#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p137#2/r2.claim: The repeated 'what' makes clear that the idol neither causes any harm nor can block benefit, and does not benefit or avert harm; blame does not require absence of both qualities together.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p137#2/r2.anchor: ولو أسقطت ( ما ) من الثاني لظن أن الذم يشترط فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p137#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p137#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p137#2/r3.claim: Calling on a powerless object is gross folly and remote misguidance: leaving its worship cannot stop God's beneficence, and worship cannot secure benefit from it or avert harm.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p137#2/r3.anchor: لأن الأول لو ترك عبادته ما قدر على منع إحسانه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p705/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p705/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p705/r1.claim: The surrounding الحج passage continues describing false deities and emphasizes their falsity, linking 22:12 with further condemnations of worshipping other than God.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p705/r1.anchor: فالكلام مستمر على ما يدعون من دون الله فأراد تعالى أن يؤكد أن هذا هو الباطل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p705/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p705/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p705/r2.claim: Samarrāʾī counts the pronoun huwa 13 times in al-Ḥajj and 7 in Luqmān, including the pronoun of separation 8 versus 3 times, to explain its heavier stylistic presence here.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p705/r2.anchor: والأمر الآخر أن الضمير (هو) من الناحية اللفظية في سمة التعبير

ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r1.claim: The phrase that the count is ten complete may seem obvious, but it prevents a mistaken reading that only seven are meant on returning.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r1.anchor: لتوهم ولو على بعد أن المراد وتمام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the claim that ʿUthmān acknowledged Qur'anic grammatical errors: it is implausible that the Companions collectively wrote, missed, and left such errors uncorrected; he calls the report weak, disrupted, and disconnected.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r2.anchor: فالحق إن ذلك لا يصح عن عثمان والخبر ضعيف مضطرب منقطع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عبد الأعلى
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r3.claim: A report says that after the codex was completed, ʿUthmān praised the work and noticed something to be corrected by their tongues; al-Ālūsī says this means they later corrected dialectal forms at review.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r3.anchor: أحسنتم وأجملتم أرى شيئا سنقيمه بألسنتنا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r4.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r4.claim: In a report al-Ālūsī calls sound on the conditions of the two Ṣaḥīḥs, ʿĀʾisha says scribes erred in writing the forms inn hādhāni, al-muqīmīn, and al-ṣābiʾūn.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r4.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه قال سألت عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها عن لحن القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī explains ʿĀʾisha's claim as choosing a less suitable dialect among the seven readings when unifying the community, not writing an impermissible error into the Qur'an.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r5.anchor: بأن معنى قولها أخطأوا أي في اختيار الأولى من الأحرف السبعة لجمع الناس عليه لا أن الذي كتبوه من ذلك خطأ

ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r6.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read al-muqīmīn al-ṣalāh and called it a scribe's grammatical error; al-Ālūsī says laḥn can mean language or reading, and notes another reading and the grammarians' analyses.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير كان يقرأ

ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r7.claim: On the no-contradiction account, the whole Qur'an is miraculous as a complete work, so sound sermons or poetry and the shortness of individual sūras do not disprove it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r7.anchor: عدم التناقض والإختلاف مع الطول والإمتداد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r8.claim: Scholars also cite the Qur'an's awe, the reciter's growing love despite repetition, its lasting presence, and God's promise to preserve it as features of its excellence.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r8.anchor: مثل الروعة التي تلحق قلوب سامعيه وأنه لا يمله تاليه بل يزداد حبا له بالترديد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r9.claim: Al-Ālūsī's own view is that the whole Qur'an, including its shortest sūra, is miraculous in its order, eloquence, unseen reports, rational accord, and subtle meaning; some aspects may be hidden while others suffice.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r9.anchor: والذي يخطر بقلب هذا الفقير أن القرآن بجملته وأبعاضه حتى أقصر سورة منه معجز بالنظر إلى نظمه وبلاغته

ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r10.claim: He closes with an unattributed line comparing successive manifestations to stars, each setting star giving way to others.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p30/r10.anchor: نجوم سماء كلما أنقض كوكب بدا كوكب تأوى إليه كواكب

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p307/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p307/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p307/r1.claim: Jurjānī rejects locating compositional thought in isolated wording: either meanings receive no thought or words are thought about apart from understood meanings, both implausible.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p307/r1.anchor: إما أن يخرج هذه المعاني من أن يكون لواضع الكلام فيها فكر

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p307/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p307/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p307/r2.claim: The speaker orders meanings before their verbal signs; words serve meanings, so their order follows the author’s thought rather than generating it for the hearer.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p307/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p307/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p307/r3.claim: A listener hears words before grasping meanings, but that cannot show that meanings are ordered from words; analysis must consider the composing speaker, not the listener.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p307/r3.anchor: والواجب أن ينظر إلى حال المعاني معه لا مع السامع

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p307/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p307/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p307/r4.claim: A Bedouin need not know formal grammatical labels to compose correctly, just as early scholars knew theological truths without later technical terms; understanding the distinctions is what matters.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p307/r4.anchor: الاعتبار بمعرفة مدلول العبارات لا بمعرفة العبارات

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p307/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p307/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p307/r5.claim: A Bedouin’s objection to the muezzin’s accusative “Muhammadan” by asking “what did he do?” shows intuitive recognition that the utterance lacked a predicate.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p307/r5.anchor: أنكر عن غير علم أن النصب يخرجه عن أن يكون خبرا
